Mandatory basic insurance 
receipt (can be submitted up 
to 3 months after entry date)
•	House search (residence 
permit)
•	Copy of employment  
contract
•	Contact details/reference 
from last lessor
 
Fill out application form and 
return/deliver it as soon as 
possible
Within a period of 14 days of 
arrival, and before taking up 
your position, you must obtain 
a residence permit from the 
municipal residents’ service of 
the town in question.
Take the following with you: 
your identity document, writ-
ten declaration of employment 
by the employer
Emigration to Switzerland 
(stays of more than 3 months).
•	Employment for fewer than 
8 hours a week = medical 
insurance includes accident 
insurance
•	Employment for more  
than 8 hours a week = the 
employer takes out accident 
insurance for you
 
Thanks to the free movement of 
people in the EU and EFTA, you 
may enter Switzerland and live 
and work here. To do so, you will 
need a valid contract of employ-
ment. 
Employment relationship from 
three months to one year
Workers are entitled to a short-
term residence permit (L EU/
EFTA), which is limited to the 
duration of the contract on the 
employment certificate.
Employment relationship from  
one to five years 
On presenting an employment 
certificate that indicates the rele-
vant duration, workers will receive 
a B EU/EFTA residence permit 
valid for five years. 
Self-employment
EU/EFTA citizens entering  
Switzerland to work as self­
employed persons will initially 
receive a B EU/EFTA residence 
permit for a period of five years, 
provided they can prove that they 
are actually working as self-em-
ployed persons at the time of 
submitting their application.
Sign the lease contract. In 
Switzerland, a deposit equal to 
one to three months’ rent must 
be paid into an account. This 
money will be returned to you 
upon leaving the house.
Taxes: the employer deducts 
taxes directly from the wages 
of workers with a B residence 
permit and transfers them to 
the tax authorities.
Take out home insurance and 
civil liability insurance. These 
insurance policies cover any 
damage to your home or any 
damage you cause to third 
parties.
Professional pension plan 
(BVG). Everybody who has 
retirement insurance must 
contribute. This money will be 
paid out to you at the end of 
your working life in Switzer-
land, or when you retire. 
Retirement insurance (AHV) is 
mandatory in Switzerland and 
is deducted directly from your 
salary.
